description: US zero-sugar wine brand whose wines carry the Clean Label Project Purity Award, sold direct through its own website with an open ambassador program for creators with 21+ audiences.

evidence.summary: Lifevine's own ambassador page states creators earn 20% commission for every order they refer, with signup and login handled through the brand's BixGrow portal (lifevinewines.bixgrow.com); the page states there is no minimum following requirement and ambassadors receive a starter bottle perk.

The same official page states twice, verbatim in substance, 'Earn 20% commission for every order you refer — no cap' — an explicit no-earnings-cap statement on the brand's own page, so commission_cap is recorded as uncapped.

name: Lifevine Wines

reasons.compensation: Published 20% commission plus an explicit 'no cap' statement on the brand's own page — top band for this group.
reasons.contact_access: A public ambassador page with signup through the brand's BixGrow portal; no public program email was published.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC wine brand with a third-party Clean Label Project Purity Award and its own storefront.
reasons.niche_fit: Zero-sugar, clean-label wine is a strong fit for food, drink and wellness creators filming tastings and swaps.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open signup with no minimum following stated; alcohol rules mean creators need 21+ audiences.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An open ambassador program with a starter-bottle perk is published on the brand's own site, though no published creator cohort size was found.

description: US ready-to-drink canned cocktail brand sold through its own website, running a brand-direct partner program for US creators aged 21+.

evidence.summary: Maux's own partner page states partners earn a flat 10% on every sale with a 60-day cookie and monthly payouts; the program is free to join with no audience minimum, is open to US creators aged 21+, and excludes holders of alcohol licenses under tied-house law.

The page's FAQ states 'There's no minimum payout threshold and no cap on what you can earn' and repeats 'paid monthly, no cap' — an explicit no-earnings-cap statement on the brand's own page, so commission_cap is recorded as uncapped.

name: Maux Cocktails

reasons.compensation: Published flat 10% on every sale with an explicit no-cap FAQ answer and no payout threshold on the brand's own page.
reasons.contact_access: A public partner page with an application form; no public program email was published.
reasons.credibility: Smaller DTC alcohol brand with its own storefront; fewer third-party credibility signals than the group's larger brands.
reasons.niche_fit: Ready-to-drink cocktails film well for drink, hosting and lifestyle creators with adult audiences.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open signup with no audience minimum; restricted to US creators 21+ and alcohol-license holders are excluded.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A public partner program aimed at creators exists on the official site, but no published creator cohort or campaign evidence was found.

description: US oral-care brand known for its coconut-oil-based dental floss and oral wellness products, sold direct through its own website.

evidence.summary: The Lasso program listing reports Cocofloss affiliates earn 20% per sale with a 30-day cookie; the listing's join link routes to ShareASale (www.shareasale.com), identifying ShareASale as the program's network. No cap statement appears in the listing, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

name: Cocofloss

reasons.compensation: Reported 20% per sale with a 30-day cookie — a high rate for this group, though reported by a third-party listing rather than the brand's own page.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through ShareASale via the program listing; no public brand program email was found.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC oral-care brand with its own storefront and retail presence.
reasons.niche_fit: A single hero oral-care product with strong visual demo potential for health and wellness creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open network application with a standard approval step.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An open network affiliate program exists, but no published creator cohort or UGC campaign evidence was found.

description: Large US men's personal care brand — natural bar soap, deodorant, shampoo and grooming products — sold direct and in retail, with a long-running affiliate program.

evidence.summary: The Lasso program listing reports Dr. Squatch affiliates earn 8% per sale with a 15-day cookie and a $50 payout threshold; the listing's join link routes to Pepperjam (id.pepperjam.com), identifying Pepperjam as the current network. An older affiliate roundup listed ShareASale for this program, which appears superseded by the current Pepperjam join route. No cap statement appears, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

name: Dr. Squatch

reasons.compensation: Reported 8% per sale with a short 15-day cookie and a $50 payout threshold — mid-to-low band for this group.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through Pepperjam via the program listing; no public brand program email was found.
reasons.credibility: Major national personal care brand with wide retail distribution and its own storefront.
reasons.niche_fit: Men's grooming staples are a proven short-form demo category, though the fit is narrower than food or supplements.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open network application with a standard approval step.
reasons.ugc_evidence: One of the most heavily creator-promoted personal care brands, with a long-running affiliate program and constant creator content.

description: Premium acupressure massage mat and set brand (Pranamat ECO), sold direct through its own website and featured in VOGUE, ELLE, Women's Health and other major publications.

evidence.summary: Pranamat's own partner portal states affiliates earn up to 10% commission on every qualifying purchase, paid monthly via PayPal or bank transfer after a 31-day validation period; the FAQ states the brand provides no complimentary products and affiliates must already own a Pranamat. The portal publishes the phone number +1 646 844 8672. No cap statement appears, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

The brand's own homepage showcases an ambassadors section with creator testimonials and press features (VOGUE, ELLE, Women's Health, The Guardian, Harper's BAZAAR), and lists a +371 (Latvia) contact number.

name: Pranamat

reasons.compensation: Published 'up to 10%' commission on the brand's own partner portal (top of range recorded; the page does not publish tier criteria).
reasons.contact_access: A public partner portal with an application flow and a published phone number, but no public program email.
reasons.credibility: Premium established brand with major-press features and a 5-year product warranty.
reasons.niche_fit: A distinctive, highly visual wellness product that demos well in recovery, sleep and self-care content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application, but affiliates must already own a Pranamat — no free products — which narrows who can start.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own homepage runs an ambassadors section full of creator testimonials, showing active creator promotion.

description: US small-batch supplement brand (probiotics, digestive enzymes and whole-food supplements) from Organic 3, sold direct through its own website.

evidence.summary: The Lasso program listing reports Smidge affiliates earn 10% per sale with a 30-day cookie; the listing's join link routes to Awin (ui.awin.com), identifying Awin as the program's network. No cap statement appears in the listing, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

The brand's own company (Organic 3) confirms on its own pages that it runs an affiliate program, describing that it works with health-conscious leaders, practitioners, doctors and influencers; the brand sells its supplement line direct through getsmidge.com.

name: Smidge

reasons.compensation: Reported 10% per sale with a 30-day cookie via a third-party listing — mid band for this group.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through Awin via the program listing; no public brand program email was found.
reasons.credibility: Established niche supplement brand with its own storefront and a long-running product line.
reasons.niche_fit: Gut-health supplements are a core wellness-creator category with strong routine-content fit.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open network application with a standard approval step.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand confirms it works with health leaders and influencers, but no published creator cohort or campaign evidence was found.

description: US zero-proof spirits-alternative brand (alcohol-free whisky, gin, vodka and other alternatives) sold through its own website, recruiting brand ambassadors.

evidence.summary: ARKAY's own brand ambassador page states ambassadors earn up to $5 per qualifying bottle sold through an apply-then-approve flow that issues a personal link; the pay is a flat per-bottle bounty rather than a percentage, so commission_rate is recorded as null with the bounty documented here. No cap statement appears on the page, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

name: ARKAY Beverages

reasons.compensation: Flat bounty of up to $5 per qualifying bottle sold (the page's 'up to' wording is documented in the evidence); no percentage rate is published.
reasons.contact_access: A public ambassador page with an application flow on the brand's own site; no public program email was recorded.
reasons.credibility: Long-running niche zero-proof brand with its own storefront; smaller public footprint than the group's larger brands.
reasons.niche_fit: Zero-proof cocktail alternatives fit the fast-growing sober-curious drink niche for food and drink creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application with a brand approval step before links are issued.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A public ambassador program exists on the official site, but no published creator cohort or campaign evidence was found.

description: US gut-health brand selling seasonal probiotics and the Jettie kids line, sold direct through its own website with an affiliate program on Rakuten Advertising.

evidence.summary: Rakuten Advertising's own advertiser spotlight confirms Jetson's affiliate program runs on the Rakuten network (publishers search MID 45524 in the publisher dashboard) and publishes the program contact email ra-jetsonaffiliate@mail.rakuten.com.

The Lasso program listing reports Jetson affiliates earn 5% per sale with a 30-day cookie, and its join link routes to Rakuten (auth.rakutenmarketing.com), corroborating the network. No cap statement appears, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

name: Jetson

reasons.compensation: Reported 5% per sale with a 30-day cookie — the lowest percentage rate in this group.
reasons.contact_access: The network's own spotlight publishes a direct program contact email — the best contact access in this group.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC gut-health brand featured in its network's own advertiser spotlight.
reasons.niche_fit: Seasonal probiotics and gut health are a core wellness-creator category with strong routine-content fit.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to Rakuten publishers via the network dashboard (MID 45524) with a standard approval step.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A live network program exists and the network spotlights the brand to publishers, but no published creator cohort evidence was found.

description: US women's health brand selling organic cotton tampons, pads, period care and personal care products by subscription and one-time purchase through its own website.

evidence.summary: RATE CONFLICT — commission_rate is recorded as null. The Lasso program listing reports 'up to 15.0%' with a 14-day cookie and a $10 payout threshold, while the Awin program description for LOLA (via affi.io) describes a flat $3–$5 per order with a 30-day cookie and coupons distributed through Pepperjam. The two sources describe materially different pay structures, so no single rate is recorded.

The Awin program description for LOLA confirms a live network affiliate program for the brand (flat per-order pay, 30-day cookie, coupon distribution via Pepperjam). No cap statement appears in either source, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

name: LOLA

reasons.compensation: No rate recorded: sources conflict between 'up to 15%' (Lasso) and a flat $3–$5 per order (Awin program description), so compensation scores low until the brand's current terms are confirmed.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through the network/listing route; no public brand program email was found.
reasons.credibility: Well-known national women's health brand with wide retail distribution and its own storefront.
reasons.niche_fit: Organic period and personal care is a strong fit for women's health creators and routine content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application; the conflicting published terms add friction a creator must resolve before promoting.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A live network affiliate program exists, but no published creator cohort or campaign evidence was found.
